item.title: Sanwo-Olu rewards Flamingos, coaches with N10m each
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded each player and member of the technical crew of Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, with N10 million following their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. In addition to the cash reward, each player received an iPhone 18 Pro Max and bespoke outfits in recognition of the team’s achievement as the first African side to win the global tournament. Sanwo-Olu announced the reward package on Sunday evening while hosting the victorious squad to a special dinner reception at the Lagos House, Marina. The governor said the gesture was in recognition of the team’s landmark victory on the global stage, which has attracted widespread acclaim across Nigeria and the African continent. The reception provided an opportunity for the Lagos State Government to celebrate the players and technical crew for bringing honour to Nigeria and making history in women’s football. item.title: Sanusi, Ladoja warn against politicising traditional institutions
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, have called for national healing, peaceful coexistence and stronger bonds among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups, warning against the politicisation of traditional institutions. The two traditional rulers spoke on Sunday in Ibadan when Sanusi paid a courtesy visit to Ladoja at his palace in Oke-Aremo, where they stressed the need for traditional institutions to remain above partisan interests and serve as instruments of reconciliation, mutual understanding and national unity. Sanusi, who was in Ibadan to honour an invitation from the League of Imams and Alfas in South-West Nigeria, said his visit reflected his belief in a country where ethnic, religious and political differences would not determine relationships among citizens. He described the engagement as one of the positive developments needed to bridge Nigeria’s regional and cultural divides, stressing that national unity, progress and prosperity could only be achieved when people from different backgrounds deliberately reached out to one another. The Emir said although other engagements had emerged, he considered it important to honour his earlier commitment to attend the conference, even if his participation would be brief. “We fixed this date a long time ago, and even though other events came, we considered it important to honour our promise to appear at the conference, even if it is for a brief period, because they have been expecting me to come. “This invitation is part of the positive developments we have been yearning for to build a bridge where Nigerians from different parts of the country reach out to each other and come together in the interest of the unity, the progress and the prosperity of our dear nation,” he said. Sanusi also apologised for the delay in visiting Ladoja following his appointment and coronation, explaining that certain circumstances had prevented him from attending earlier. He congratulated Ladoja on his ascension to the throne of his forebears and prayed for divine protection, a long and peaceful reign, as well as prosperity for Ibadanland and Nigeria. The Emir described the courtesy visit as necessary, given the longstanding relationship between the two traditional institutions and their respective communities. Reflecting on his relationship with Ibadan, Sanusi recalled his longstanding connections with the ancient city dating back to his days at First Bank, his association with the late Aare Musulumi of Yorubaland, Alhaji Abdulazeez Arisekola Alao, and his subsequent tenure as Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria. He said Ibadan had remained a familiar destination over the years, adding that he had maintained close relationships with several indigenes of the city. item.title: NDC candidate in Kwara pledges N120,000 minimum wage for workers
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kwara, Prof. Abdulmumin Ajia, has pledged a minimum wage of N120,000 for workers in the state. Ajia made the pledge on Sunday in Ilorin while unveiling the NDC’s 2027 Gubernatorial Campaign Council manifesto, tagged ‘Forward Kwara Agenda’. He proposed a N120,000 public-service minimum wage benchmark and a cost-of-living adjustment framework for workers and pensioners. He said his administration would verify the payroll, assess the financial implications, consult labour unions and publish an implementation and funding timetable. On pensioners, Ajia promised to verify outstanding gratuities and publish a schedule for settling validated arrears. He also pledged to establish a predictable payment timetable for newly due pension obligations. Ajia said he entered the governorship race to make public institutions work reliably for all Kwarans, regardless of political affiliation. “I am running to make public institutions work that way. If entrusted with office, I will serve people who support me, people who oppose me and people who have never attended a political meeting,” he said. He said his experience as a teacher, researcher and university administrator had taught him to ask critical questions, examine evidence and take responsibility for results. Ajia, who led a School of Business and mentored young people, said his visits home exposed him to the challenges facing unemployed graduates. He said many young people could hardly predict when fair employment opportunities would become available. According to him, government has a responsibility to ensure that citizens understand how to access assistance, eligibility requirements and appeal procedures. He said access to public services should not depend on personal relationships with the governor. Ajia said the Forward Kwara Agenda outlined six areas of governance, anchored on stronger institutions, greater opportunities and shared prosperity. On security, he said farmers should access their farms, children should travel safely to school and traders should return home safely from markets. NAN reports that the event attracted hundreds of NDC stakeholders from the state’s 16 local government areas. item.title: ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach
item.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp praised Xavi Hernandez on Sunday, saying the new Netherlands coach already had the Dutch playing in his own image after just five games in charge. Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s meeting between the two old rivals, Klopp pointed to Friday’s 7-0 thumping of Greece in Amsterdam and said the former midfielder had made an impression. Considered among the best midfielders in the history of the game, Xavi formed the core of a possession-dominant Barcelona side who won four Champions League titles. He also won the World Cup with Spain. “They simply played some electric football,” Klopp said, adding: “Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football… “He’s a coach who really pushes his approach to the limit. And that’s exciting. I always loved playing against teams who play like this.” Third in the group with only the top two reaching the quarter-finals, Germany will need to beat the Netherlands to give themselves a chance. “They’re a team who really come alive in European football,” Klopp said of the Netherlands. “It’s one of the fiercest rivalries in football. It’s a great honour for me.” Appointed in August, the Spaniard said he was beginning to understand the nature of the rivalry with Germany. “Now I can understand more because I’m here and I feel this kind of rivalry. It will be a really good test for us,” Xavi said. In his press conference, Xavi deflected Klopp’s praise and said the Netherlands’ big win over Greece was down to his players. “It’s not Xavi-football. It’s all about the players. They are the most important. I don’t need to convince them to play this style of football, they have the capacity to play like the last game. Germany and the Netherlands played out a 1-1 draw in Amsterdam in September, the first match in charge for both Klopp and Xavi. Xavi said he would try and do the unexpected on Monday, but acknowledged it would not be easy against the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach. “It’s difficult to surprise a coach like Jurgen Klopp,” Xavi said. “He’s one of the best coaches in the past few years. And it’s an honour to come up against him tomorrow.” Vanguard News The post ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: NDC accuses Tinubu of prioritising campaign propaganda over budgets
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of prioritising campaign propaganda and political patronage over funding critical sectors of the economy, alleging that the huge spending on political publicity explains the poor implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets. The opposition party challenged the Federal Government to publish verifiable figures showing how much had been released for critical capital projects and administrative subventions in the three fiscal years, compared with expenditure on political advertisements and patronage. The NDC made the allegations in a statement signed on Sunday by the Spokesperson of its National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, titled, “Dear Mr. President: The Huge Cost of Your Campaign Propaganda Testifies to Why You Failed to Adequately Fund 2024, 2025 and 2026 Budgets.” The party said its assessment of what it described as a barrage of political advertisements, donations, vehicles, laptops, sewing machines, food items and other gifts distributed by groups and individuals claiming to support Tinubu had raised questions about the administration’s spending priorities. It alleged that despite increased government revenue following the removal of fuel subsidy and higher taxation, critical social and physical infrastructure, national security and citizens’ welfare had not received adequate funding. Ikokwu said: “For instance, despite the palpable insecurity confronting the nation, only about seven per cent of the Defence Capital Budget was reportedly released in 2025. “Even more disturbing was when the Minister of Health reported that only ₦36 million out of the ₦218 billion allocated to Health Capital expenditure was released in the same 2025.” The party argued that the alleged low releases for defence and health raised questions about the government’s commitment to addressing insecurity and improving public services. It also expressed concern over the implementation of the 2026 budget, which it claimed had received inadequate attention, and accused the APC of devoting substantial resources to campaign publicity and political patronage ahead of the 2027 elections. Questioning the administration’s spending priorities, Ikokwu asked how a government benefiting from fuel subsidy removal and increased taxation could plead a lack of funds for national security, healthcare, education, federal roads and the welfare of ordinary Nigerians while political activities appeared to attract substantial resources. The NDC also alleged that several state governments, particularly those it claimed had been pressured into joining the APC, had poor records of budget implementation but had sufficient resources for campaign propaganda. item.title: Gridlock as multiple trailers crash on Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
item.description: …Inward-Lagos carriageway blocked at Kara Bridge By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Traffic was brought to a standstill on Sunday evening following a multiple-trailer crash around Kara Bridge, near Ibafo, on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The accident blocked the inward-Lagos carriageway, leaving motorists stranded as emergency responders and traffic officials battled to clear the wreckage. A trailer with an unknown registration number was seen overturned on its side, with its container crushed and contents scattered across the road, while other trailers were rammed into one another behind it. Officials of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, and other emergency personnel were at the scene directing traffic, controlling onlookers and coordinating clearance operations. A heavy-duty tow truck and payloader were also deployed to remove the wrecked vehicles and restore traffic movement. The crash attracted dozens of onlookers, while vehicles on the opposite carriageway moved slowly as motorists attempted to catch a glimpse of the accident scene. Efforts to clear the affected carriageway were ongoing as of press time. Motorists travelling towards Lagos from Ibafo, Mowe and adjoining areas were advised to exercise patience, drive cautiously around the scene and explore alternative routes where possible. The cause of the crash and whether there were casualties had yet to be established as of the time of filing this report. item.title: 2027: Ex-FCT minister Akinjide backs Tinubu, Alli
item.description: Former Minister of State for the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Oloye Jumoke Akinjide, has declared her support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid and the governorship ambition of Senator Sharafadeen Alli in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 general elections. Her Special Assistant, Olatundun Gabriel, announced the development in a statement, indicating the former minister’s renewed political engagement under the banner of Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Gabriel, a former Chief of Staff to the Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, also unveiled the slogan, “JUMOKE IS COMING — RENEWED HOPE 2027”, declaring the commencement of a fresh political engagement. “We are pleased to announce that the journey to renewed service has begun,” he said. He said Akinjide’s political engagement would align with Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and the governorship ambition of Alli, urging her supporters across Oyo State and beyond to remain united and committed. “As we align with the Renewed Hope Agenda of our Leader and Father, His Excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, and with the vision of our Gubernatorial Candidate, Distinguished Senator Sharafadeen Alli, we urge all supporters across Oyo State and beyond to remain steadfast, united, prayerful and focused,” Gabriel stated. He also appreciated Akinjide’s political associates for their longstanding loyalty and support, assuring them that further directives and engagements would follow. The declaration comes amid political realignments in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 elections, as the All Progressives Congress, APC, prepares to challenge the Allied People’s Movement, APM, for control of the state. Akinjide, a former federal cabinet member with longstanding political connections in Oyo State, is expected to bring her political experience and network into the emerging APC mobilisation efforts. Her declaration of support for Tinubu and Alli signals her involvement in the political contest ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: FG settles ₦1.23trn electricity debt, says Power Minister
item.description: …2.8m customers metered, transmission capacity rises by 1,300MVA The Minister of Power, Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, has said the Federal Government has settled ₦1.23 trillion out of the ₦3.3 trillion approved by President Bola Tinubu for the payment of verified legacy debts owed to electricity generation companies. Tegbe also disclosed that more than 2.8 million electricity customers had been metered between 2023 and October 2026 under the Presidential Metering Initiative. The minister made the disclosures on Friday at an interactive luncheon with senior editors in Lagos, where he reaffirmed the Tinubu administration’s commitment to improving electricity supply through sustained reforms, infrastructure investment and better service delivery. He acknowledged Nigerians’ frustration over unreliable electricity supply but said the government was addressing the sector’s longstanding challenges through coordinated interventions. According to him, the challenges include gas supply constraints, ageing infrastructure, vandalism, transmission limitations, inadequate metering and commercial difficulties across the electricity value chain. He said the interconnected nature of the problems required disciplined implementation of reforms rather than isolated interventions or short-term solutions. Highlighting progress in the transmission segment, Tegbe said recently commissioned substations and equipment had added more than 1,300 megavolt-amperes, MVA, to the national transmission capacity. He listed the locations covered by the improvements to include Apapa, Ijora, Ikeja, Kumbotoso, Dankata, Mashi, Dan-Agundi, Biliri and Walalambe. The minister also disclosed that the government was building a new National Grid Control Centre in Osogbo to replace the existing facility, which is more than 60 years old. He said the government was also working towards expanding electricity generation capacity to 10,000 megawatts. On the ministry’s development strategy, Tegbe identified the Lagos-Ogun, Benin-Enugu-Port Harcourt and Abuja-Kaduna-Kano economic corridors as priority energy zones. He explained that the Lagos-Ogun axis and Abuja franchise area, which together account for more than 50 per cent of national electricity demand, had been identified as proposed pilot locations for 24-hour energy zones, subject to technical readiness and commercial viability. The initiative, he said, was aimed at aligning electricity generation, transmission and distribution capacity with demand in major economic centres. On the protection of electricity infrastructure, Tegbe said the Federal Government had approved a coordinated anti-vandalism campaign involving relevant security agencies, alongside stronger legal measures to safeguard critical power assets. The minister also sought a stronger partnership with the media, stressing the need for factual reporting, professional scrutiny and transparent communication of government interventions. item.title: Gov Mbah: How Tinubu’s reforms halted Nigeria’s economic collapse
item.description: …Says shared prosperity follows Governor of Enugu State, Dr. Peter Mbah, says Nigeria would have suffered total economic collapse but for President Bola Tinubu’s courageous reforms, arguing that the removal of fuel subsidy and floating of the naira only waited until the President’s assumption of office in 2023 because the nation delayed the ‘evil day’ and lived on borrowed time. He gave the insights at the weekend during the launch of “As Tinubu Mbah Moves” (ATM), a support group convened by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh (SAN), and dedicated to the re-election of President Tinubu and Governor Mbah in Enugu. Speaking to the mammoth crowd, he said, “It would have been a lot easier for any leader to just continue with the status quo and carry on on the basis of business as usual. But for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, it was business unusual that led to the bold initiatives. “As a person who had played very actively in the oil and gas sector, I had written quite a lot of features and articles arguing against the fuel subsidy regime long before now, for it was clear to me, even from the point of a major player in that sector, that the subsidy regime was not sustainable because of the economic devastation it was causing to us as Nigerians. We were just basically postponing the evil day. “We were just digging our poverty pits continually. We were actually digging deeper into that pit of poverty. And it would have taken a very courageous leader in his first term to say, ‘Look, if we have to build for the future, if we have to think about our children, then we must take out the subsidy and we must also unify the exchange rate regime.’” Mbah took a swipe at the foreign exchange regime before the floating of the naira by Tinubu, describing it as a cesspool of corruption. “We got to a point in this country where even salary earners, once they get paid, would run to the bureau de change to change it rather than hold their salary in naira. Confidence was completely eroded in the naira. Nobody wanted to touch it with the tip of their finger. And that was the recipe for a failed nation. “If you wanted to do a study or research of any failed nation, it is when the country, the citizens themselves, begin to lose confidence in their currency. And that was the environment that this President inherited. “It was a major cesspool of corruption. The arbitrage was obvious and people were being taken advantage of. What was happening between the official and the parallel market was terrible. And some people were benefiting from that arbitrage at the expense of the economy. But it took this President’s understanding of the economy to be able to make those bold decisions,” he explained. item.title: Photos: Ronaldinho returns to professional football at age 46
item.description: Greying and rounder in the face than during his prime, Ronaldinho made a winning return to professional football on Sunday for Ravenna, an ambitious club in Italy’s third tier aiming to reach Serie A. Under the watchful eye of Ignazio Cipriani, the Italian-American businessman who has owned the club since 2024, Ronaldinho perfectly played his role as the centrepiece of a clever PR stunt. Brazilian football star Ronaldinho waves to supporters at half-time during the Italian Serie C football match between Ravenna and Forli at the Benelli stadium in Ravenna on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Stefano RELLANDINI / AFP) The 46-year-old Brazilian great put in a low-key performance in his first competitive match since playing for Fluminense in 2015, as Ravenna, bidding for promotion to Serie B, beat local rivals Forli 2-0 in front of a packed Stadio Bruno Benelli on Italy’s Adriatic coast. Ravenna’s Giulio Donati (L) celebrates after scoring with Brazilian football star Ronaldinho (top) during the Italian Serie C football match between Ravenna and Forli at the Benelli stadium in Ravenna on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Stefano RELLANDINI / AFP) Known for his dynamic dribbling and often outrageous ball control in his heyday, Ronaldinho largely strolled around the pitch and laid off simple passes to his teammates, who would once upon a time not have been anywhere near his level as players. Ronaldinho’s arrival has given Ravenna a previously unimaginable profile, and Cipriani would no doubt have been delighted to see the pack of reporters and photographers that descended on the Benelli. Brazilian football star Ronaldinho looks on during the Italian Serie C football match between Ravenna and Forli at the Benelli stadium in Ravenna on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Stefano RELLANDINI / AFP) The 2005 Ballon d’Or winner only played in the first half but was involved in the move which ended with Giulio Donati smashing hosts Ravenna ahead in the 36th minute. Ronaldinho entered the field to great fanfare, with the 5,000-capacity Benelli having a temporary stand with 1,800 places — dubbed “R10” — added for the occasion. Brazilian football star Ronaldinho answers journalists at half-time during the Italian Serie C football match between Ravenna and Forli at the Benelli stadium in Ravenna on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Stefano Rellandini / AFP) Flares and smoke bombs were let off in the stands while Andrea Bocelli’s “Con Te Partiro” blasting out of the stadium’s speakers. And he left after the first half, but not before plenty of handshakes with his teammates and match officials. Only he knows whether he will play for Ravenna again, although he had only taken part in a single training session with his teammates before this one-off appearance. He only arrived in Italy a few days before Sunday’s match, suggesting that he hasn’t committed himself for the long haul. item.title: My relationship with Kogi Central goes beyond elections – Natasha
item.description: John Alechenu Senator Natasha Hadiza Akpoti-Uduaghanb has kickstarted her 2027 re-election campaign with a clear call to her constituents: vote, and be prepared to protect your votes. Speaking with confidence about her re-election bid, the federal lawmaker said her relationship with the people of Kogi Central Senatorial District went beyond elections. Her Media Aide, Sam Idoko, in a statement on Sunday, quoted her as telling thousands of supporters at a campaign event in Ihima: “My relationship with the people of Kogi Central goes beyond elections. These are my people, my family and the very reason I remain committed to public service. I do not need an election season to remember where I come from.” The campaign commenced in October with roadside receptions across Okene and adjoining areas before culminating in a major gathering at her residence in Obeiba, Ihima, Okehi Local Government Area. The motorcade passed through Itakpe, Kabba Junction, Ogaminana, the PDP Secretariat, Agassa Roundabout and Obehira. At every stop, residents and party faithful lined the route to welcome her. In Ihima, thousands gathered and many stayed late into the night. More than 500 supporters travelled from Abuja to be there. Her husband, High Chief Emmanuel Uduaghan, was beside her. Alhaji MJ Akpata Aliu was present. PDP candidates for the House of Representatives in Adavi/Okehi, Ajaokuta and Okene/Ogori-Magongo, and candidates for the State Assembly, also attended. Natasha said, “What we witnessed today is a reflection of the bond we have continued to build over time. I am deeply grateful to everyone who came out, not because they were compelled to do so, but because they believe in the journey we have undertaken together.” In Ajaokuta and Geregu, she tied her second-term bid to her first-term record. “I will not take the massive support I am enjoying from you for granted. Leadership comes with responsibility. We are campaigning on the strength of what we have achieved in the past and what I will do when given the opportunity again,” she said. At Ajaokuta Ward, she urged support for all PDP candidates and listened to Fulani communities asking for solar streetlights, boreholes and school blocks. She assured them their concerns would receive attention. “You must vote and defend your votes,” she said, urging constituents to watch the proper recording and uploading of results and the use of BVAS. Across the five local government areas, Adavi, Ajaokuta, Okehi, Okene and Ogori-Magongo, her campaign is built on work already done: water projects, solar streetlights, school devices, market infrastructure, digital connectivity and support for small businesses. In Ajaokuta Steel City, she donated learning iPads to Comprehensive Secondary School. In Adavi, on November 2, she took smart devices and laptops to OCSS Oboroke, Adavi Model Secondary School, Adavi Eba, and Community Secondary School, Obangede. item.title: FG eliminates 15,000 terrorists in 3yrs as 130,000 Boko Haram fighters surrender – APC-PCC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC on Sunday dusclosed that the military has eliminated more than 15,000 Boko Haram terrorists and bandits in the last three years, while more than 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and dependents have surrendered. Council Spokesperson, Dele Alake, said in a statement that the figures come from the scale of President Bola Tinubu’s ongoing military operations across the country. The President, he said, is determined to end the 17-year scourge of insecurity ravaging parts of Nigeria through a Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan. The fighters and dependents surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the Federal Government’s rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents. According to the statement, “the figures underscore the administration’s two-phase approach of sustained military operations and non-kinetic interventions to address insecurity.” The plan, it said, “provides a long-term framework for aligning defence priorities, operational requirements, capability development, and expenditure with Nigeria’s current and anticipated security challenges.” The statement described the initiative as a major component of the President’s determination to reposition the security architecture toward “a more coordinated, intelligence-led, technology-enabled, and prevention-oriented system capable of addressing terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, and other forms of criminality.” On the military’s structure, the statement said President Tinubu has created four new Army divisions and restructured existing formations. The reforms, it said, “aim to expand operational coverage, decentralise military operations, and enable troops to respond more swiftly to security threats across the country.” The President has also approved two additional Army depots, in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State. Each can accommodate 6,000 recruits at a time, giving a combined training capacity of 12,000 soldiers. The Osogbo facility’s capacity is already being demonstrated, with 5,210 recruits currently undergoing training there. The expansion is expected “to reduce recruit turnaround time and increase the number of soldiers available for deployment.” President Tinubu has also approved the recruitment of an additional 28,000 soldiers “to strengthen the military’s presence on the ground and enhance its operational effectiveness.” He approved the recruitment of 50,000 additional police officers as well, to reinforce internal security and improve policing capacity. item.title: Mammoth crowd welcomes Wali as Buni empowers over 500 youths, women in Yobe South
item.description: There was a mammoth crowd in Gadaka, Fika Local Government Area of Yobe State, on Thursday as the state government distributed empowerment items to over 500 youths and women across Yobe South Senatorial District (Zone B). The beneficiaries, drawn from the four local government areas in the zone, received motorcycles, tricycles (Jega) and sewing machines. The empowerment is aimed at promoting economic inclusion, supporting small businesses and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities. Beneficiaries and stakeholders at the event expressed appreciation for the intervention, saying it would boost economic activities at the grassroots. They also reaffirmed their support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Governor Mai Mala Buni and the All Progressives Congress (APC), citing investments in road infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and peacebuilding across their communities. Speaking at the event, the APC governorship candidate in the state, Hon. Baba Mallam Wali, commended Governor Buni’s economic empowerment initiatives and pledged to sustain and consolidate them if elected in the 2027 general elections. Wali said the programme would be expanded to reach more youths and women across the state. Party leaders at the event also reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening party unity and working for the success of the APC at all levels, from the State House of Assembly to the Presidency.

item.title: 2027 Grammys Nominations To Be Announced Monday
item.description: Nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, scheduled to hold in February 2027, will be announced on Monday, November 16, with Nigerian music fans able to follow the presentation from 1:45 p.m. West African Time (WAT). The Recording Academy will unveil nominees across all 100 categories during a special presentation led by its Chief Executive Officer, Harvey Mason Jr., and Chair of its Board of Trustees, Dr Chelsey Green. The announcement will begin at 7:45 a.m. Eastern Time (1:45 p.m. WAT), while the complete list of nominees is expected to be published around 9 a.m. Eastern Time (3 p.m. WAT). The presentation will be streamed live on Grammy.com and the official Grammys YouTube channel, with additional coverage on ABC’s Good Morning America. Grammys For the first time, the nominations presentation will also be broadcast live at The Square in Times Square, New York, in partnership with Hilton, the Recording Academy’s official hotel partner. Several Grammy-winning and nominated artistes are expected to join Mason and Green in announcing the nominees. They include Alan Menken, Amy Allen, Carly Pearce, David Guetta, FYÜTCH and Aura V, Herbie Hancock, Israel Houghton, Juanes, Kehlani, Linda Perry, Meghan Foley and Michelle Holme, Olivia Dean, Pharrell Williams, Renée Fleming, YUNGBLUD and Ziggy Marley. New Categories The 2027 edition introduces five new award categories, bringing the total number of categories to 100. They are Best Asian Pop Music Performance, Best Latin Song, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, and Best Traditional Folk Album. The eligibility period for the awards covers recordings released between August 31, 2025, and August 28, 2026. LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – FEBRUARY 01: (FOR EDITORIAL USE ONLY) Olivia Dean attends the 68th GRAMMY Awards at Crypto.com Arena on February 01, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Amy Sussman/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Amy Sussman / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) The Recording Academy conducted the first round of voting between October 12 and 22, 2026, while final-round voting is scheduled to run from December 10, 2026, to January 7, 2027. Ahead of the nominations, artistes including Olivia Dean, Kehlani, Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo, Bruno Mars and Rosalía have featured prominently in predictions and discussions surrounding potential contenders. item.title: Bloody Spit: Ghana Waste Dump Poses Health, Environmental ‘Crisis’
item.description: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana’s capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water. At Agbogbloshie, a district on the Korle Lagoon delta, thousands of tonnes of refuse have accumulated over decades, overwhelming the fragile wetlands overlooking a slum of around 80,000 residents, many of them migrants and traders. For scrap dealer James Hassan, a 31-year-old Liberian immigrant, it is both his home and livelihood. Without gloves or a mask, he sifts daily through piles of unwanted electronics and metal for scraps to sell. The skin on his palms is thickened and scarred from cuts and rashes but he has become accustomed to the pain and discomfort. “I have headaches and coughs after long days under the sun, but I have never sought medical care. I feel they are normal,” he told AFP. Environmental health experts say that workers are exposed to toxic metals and chemicals through skin cuts, inhaling waste smoke and dust. Waste collectors dig through piles of waste at the Agbogbloshie dumpsite in Accra, on September 28, 2026. Photo by NIPAH DENNIS / AFP While no study as yet links specific diseases to Agbogbloshie’s pollution, “the cumulative contamination raises concern even if precise causal chains remain unquantified,” epidemiologist Reginald Quansah, of the University of Ghana, said. Global Pipeline Of Waste Waste management is a prominent theme at the COP31 climate talks, which began in Turkey on Monday. Agbogbloshie’s refuse comes largely from beyond Ghana’s borders. Accra’s huge second-hand clothing market has imports from Europe, North America and Asia — but often with a troubling byproduct. “A lot of clothes that are shipped into Ghana come as waste,” Greenpeace Africa’s head of investigations Samuel Quashie-Idun told AFP. Greenpeace estimates that 15 million used garments arrive in Ghana each week. Even after traders extract what they can sell, roughly half ends up as “dead waste” dumped on beaches and fields or burned, it said. One study Greenpeace cited put Ghana’s used clothing imports at over 110,000 tonnes in 2022. For the country’s 35 million people, “these volumes far exceed local demand and… burdens waste systems,” Quashie-Idun said. Greenpeace found that 89 percent of sampled “dead” garments contained petrochemical fibres such as polyester, which shed microplastics as they decay, and release carcinogens hundreds of times above safe levels in smoke when the textiles are burned. “This is not just an environmental crisis… it’s also a human health crisis,” said Hellen Kahaso Dena, Greenpeace’s plastics project expert. ‘Fashion Waste Dumping Ground’ “The global north is effectively using Ghana as a dumping ground for fashion waste,” she told AFP. item.title: Cabo Verde Votes In Presidential Election As Incumbent Seeks Second Term
item.description: Cabo Verde voted for a new president on Sunday, with incumbent Jose Maria Neves favoured to win a second term as head of state of the West African archipelago renowned for its democratic stability. He is facing the country’s first woman candidate, Joana Rosa Amado, among other contenders. Voting started at 0900 GMT and ends at 1900 GMT. Provisional results are expected overnight. “I’ve voted. Now I’m going to mass, and I believe everything will go well — normally and with civic-mindedness,” Adilia Gomes, 55, told AFP after casting her ballot in the capital, Praia. “Everything went normally despite a few minutes’ delay in the opening of my polling station,” added another voter, Claudino Semedo. Nearly 420,000 people are eligible to vote. The election is being watched by about 150 observers from the Economic Community of West African States, the African Union and European Union. A supporter of Cape Verde’s President and presidential candidate Jose Maria Neves waves a flag bearing his image during a campaign rally in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on October 30, 2026.(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) Cabo Verde, located in the Atlantic Ocean about 600 kilometres (375 miles) off the coast of Senegal, comprises 10 volcanic islands and is an increasingly popular tourist destination. It made world headlines this year when its national football team reached the knockout stages in its first World Cup, and when a cruise ship containing people with hantavirus docked off its shores. Stability, Hospitality Unlike several of its West African neighbours where presidential elections have been tense in recent years, Cabo Verde is known for its political stability and good governance. It is considered a model of democracy in Africa, with strong economic growth. A voter queues at a polling station during Cape Verde’s presidential election in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on November 15, 2026(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) The country is known for its “morabeza” (“hospitality”, in local creole), openness, and carnivals. It also has its own style of music. According to the Mo Ibrahim Foundation 2026 index on global governance, Cabo Verde ranks third out of 54 countries on the continent. Politically, it has a semi-presidential system in which the executive is dominated by the prime minister. The president does not govern but acts more as an arbiter, working to guarantee unity and uphold the constitution. The head of state appoints the prime minister based on the results of legislative elections and represents the country abroad. item.title: Fela, Queen Latifah, Phil Collins Join Rock Hall Of Fame
item.description: Afrobeat pioneer Fela Kuti, rhapsodic hip-hop transformers Wu-Tang Clan and punk rocker Billy Idol were among the music luminaries inducted Saturday into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame at a star-studded concert gala. The versatile Phil Collins, post-punk and electronic dance music renegades Joy Division/New Order, and the velvet-voiced late Luther Vandross also joined the rock pantheon at the ceremony held in Los Angeles’s Peacock Theater. But several of the 2026 class of artists — Oasis, Sade and Iron Maiden — skipped the night celebrating their honor, one of the music industry’s most prestigious. But the show went on. Staten Island’s own Wu-Tang Clan — the ragtag group of New Yorkers who paired raw production with streetwise rhymes and martial arts influences — brought the ruckus, performing their own hits including “C.R.E.A.M” and “Wu‐Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” “We went from being banned on the radio to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame,” said member Method Man onstage to resounding cheers. To the haters, he said, “you can kiss my inducted ass.” It proved a banner night for women in hip-hop, with honorees including Queen Latifah as well as MC Lyte, who is widely recognized as the “First Lady of Hip Hop.” The storied performers tore up the stage with a medley of their hits, before Megan Thee Stallion and Remy Ma joined them to underscore the legacy of women in rap. Travis Barker, the drummer from Blink-182, inducted Collins, drawing tears from the British artist who attended the ceremony alongside his children, including Lily of “Emily in Paris” fame. US rapper/actress Queen Latifah attends the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on November 14, 2026. (Photo by VALERIE MACON / AFP) Collins — whose entry into the hall is his second, the first was as part of the band Genesis — walked to the stage with two canes, taking the mic and saying, “I’m really not as bad as it looks.” “You haven’t heard the last of me, I can promise you that.” Cynthia Erivo belted out Collins’s smash “In The Air Tonight,” with Barker playing the instantly recognizable drum fill. “My life has just been one thing after the other, one dream after the other,” Collins said to journalists backstage.
